examDifficulty.heading: Is the MuleSoft Developer I Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: The Salesforce Certified MuleSoft Developer exam covers basic Mule 4 projects, Anypoint Platform and Studio, integrations, DataWeave, event flow, error handling, and batch processing.
bullets: 60 multiple-choice questions, plus up to five unscored questions in 120 minutes.
The official guide describes experience with basic Mule 4 projects under guidance and supervision; it does not specify a minimum number of projects or a required prior certification.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Use the official objective list to plan practice in Anypoint Studio, DataWeave, integration design, error handling, and deployment.

examFormat.heading: MuleSoft Developer I Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or in-person. Here is the format:
bestWayToPass: Master DataWeave 2.0: Practice map, filter, reduce, and pluck functions until you can read and write scripts fluently.
Build flows in Anypoint Studio: Create HTTP-triggered flows with database and Salesforce connectors, error handling, and deployment to CloudHub.
Know your connectors: Understand HTTP Listener vs Request, Database operations, and how to configure the Salesforce connector for CRUD.
Understand error handling: Know when to use On Error Continue vs On Error Propagate and how the error type hierarchy works.

certificationCard.description: This credential validates skills to design, build, test, debug, deploy, and manage basic APIs and integrations using Mule 4 and Anypoint Platform.
topics: Deploying and Managing APIs and Integrations (7%)

keyConcepts.h2: MuleSoft Developer I: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Official credential and exam details
blocks.body: Salesforce currently lists the credential as [Salesforce Certified MuleSoft Developer](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/credentials/mulesoftdeveloperi). The available [official exam guide](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=005298959&language=en_US&type=1) lists 60 multiple-choice questions and up to five unscored questions, 120 minutes, a 70% passing score, USD 200 registration, USD 100 retake, and no prerequisite; however, its stated exam alignment is Spring ’24. Confirm the current outline before booking, and check [Salesforce certification pricing](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=005298916&language=en_US&type=1). The credential is a prerequisite for MuleSoft Developer II.

blocks.heading: Anypoint Platform and Development Lifecycle
blocks.body: **Anypoint Platform** is MuleSoft's integration platform — Design, Develop, Deploy, Manage. **Anypoint Studio** is the Eclipse-based IDE for Mule application development. Anypoint Exchange is the asset repository for APIs, connectors, templates, and examples. **CloudHub** is the iPaaS (integration Platform as a Service) for deploying Mule apps. The developer lifecycle: design the API spec in API Designer → publish to Exchange → implement in Studio → deploy to CloudHub → manage in Runtime Manager.

blocks.heading: Mule Events, Flows, and Core Concepts
blocks.body: A Mule Event carries the message through the flow: Payload (the message data), Attributes (metadata about the source, like HTTP headers), Variables (flow-level storage), Error (in error handling context). A Flow has a Source (event trigger — HTTP listener, file listener, scheduler), Processors (transform, route, call), and Target (destination system). Sub-flows are reusable flow fragments without a source. Private flows can be called but not directly triggered. The developer exam tests Mule event structure and when to use each flow type.

blocks.heading: DataWeave 2.0 Transformations
blocks.body: **DataWeave** is MuleSoft's transformation language — used to transform, filter, and map data. Key operators: map (transform array elements), filter (select matching elements), reduce (aggregate), pluck (transform object entries), groupBy (group array by key). Type system: String, Number, Boolean, Array, Object, Null, Any. Header declarations define input/output MIME types. %dw 2.0 output application/json --- means DataWeave version 2, output format JSON. The exam tests reading and writing DataWeave scripts for common transformation scenarios.

blocks.heading: API Design with RAML and API-First
blocks.body: RAML 1.0 (RESTful API Modeling Language) defines API contracts. Structure: baseUri, version, mediaType, types (data types), traits (reusable method fragments), resourceTypes (reusable resource patterns). API Fragment types in Exchange: data types, traits, resource types, security schemes, examples. API-first development: design and mock the API spec, share with consumers for feedback, then implement. Mocking Service in Exchange lets consumers test against the spec before implementation is complete. The exam tests RAML syntax and API-first methodology.

blocks.heading: Error Handling: On Error Continue vs Propagate
blocks.body: Error handling in Mule uses Try scope, On Error Continue, and On Error Propagate. On Error Continue: catches the error, executes the handler, and resumes the flow after the error scope — the client receives the handler's response. On Error Propagate: catches the error, executes the handler, and re-throws the error — the client receives an error response. Error types follow a hierarchy: ANY (catch all), CONNECTIVITY, EXPRESSION, ROUTING, SECURITY. The exam tests which handler type is appropriate and how error types are matched.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the MuleSoft Developer I Exam
scenarioTips.intro: The MuleSoft Developer I exam tests foundational Anypoint Platform skills: building integrations in Anypoint Studio, using connectors, transforming data with DataWeave, and deploying to CloudHub. Focus on practical flow design and DataWeave syntax.

blocks.heading: Mule 4 Flow Design
blocks.body: Know the three flow types: Flow (with message source), Sub-Flow (no source, called by reference), and Private Flow. Understand the flow lifecycle and how the Mule Message (payload, attributes, variables) changes through processors.

blocks.heading: DataWeave 2.0 Fundamentals
blocks.body: **DataWeave** is the transformation language at the core of Mule 4. Know how to map, filter, transform, and coerce data types. Key functions: map, filter, mapObject, reduce, pluck, flatten, and type coercion operators.

blocks.heading: Core Connectors
blocks.body: Know the key connectors: HTTP Listener/Request, Database, File/FTP, JMS/AMQP, Salesforce, and how to configure each. Understand connection pooling, reconnection strategies, and connection testing.

blocks.heading: Error Handling
blocks.body: Know the error handling mechanisms: Try/Catch scope, On Error Continue vs. On Error Propagate, and Global Error Handlers. Understand error type hierarchy (MULE:CONNECTIVITY, HTTP:UNAUTHORIZED, etc.) and how to handle them.

blocks.heading: Deployment to CloudHub
blocks.body: Know how to deploy a Mule application to **CloudHub** 1.0: environment selection, worker configuration (size and count), deployment properties, and how to monitor deployed applications.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Next Certifications After Developer
nextCertsAfter.intro: After this certification, common next steps in the developer track:

sampleQuestions.question: An error occurs in a flow and the developer wants the flow to recover and return a successful result to the caller. Which scope should be used?
sampleQuestions.explanation: On Error Continue handles the error and lets the owning flow complete successfully, returning the handler's result.
whyWrong: Until Successful retries an operation rather than shaping the error outcome.
A Try scope without a handler does not change the outcome.
On Error Propagate re-throws to the caller after handling, so the caller sees a failure.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a Mule event consist of?
options: Only the payload and nothing else
The connectors configured in the project
A message with payload and attributes, plus variables
A payload plus a reference to the flow
sampleQuestions.explanation: The event carries the message, which holds payload and attributes, alongside any variables set in the flow.
whyWrong: Attributes and variables are part of the event as well as the payload.
Connectors are configuration, not event content.
Flow references are components, not parts of the event.

sampleQuestions.question: A DataWeave script must output JSON from an incoming XML payload. Which directive sets the output type?
sampleQuestions.explanation: The DataWeave header declares the output MIME type, which determines how the result is written.
whyWrong: Setting the payload does not declare a MIME type for serialisation.
Reconnection strategies deal with connectivity failures.
Input type is usually inferred and does not control output.

sampleQuestions.question: Which DataWeave operator applies a transformation to every item in an array?
sampleQuestions.explanation: map returns a new array with the transformation applied to each element.
whyWrong: filter selects a subset without transforming the items.
reduce collapses the array to a single accumulated value.
groupBy reorganises items into an object keyed by an expression.

sampleQuestions.question: What distinguishes attributes from variables in a Mule event?
options: Attributes survive across flows but variables do not
Attributes are set by each operation; variables persist
sampleQuestions.explanation: Attributes are metadata produced by the source or operation and are overwritten by each one. Variables are set deliberately and persist through the flow.
whyWrong: They have different lifecycles and uses.
Variables propagate through flow references, so this is the wrong way round.
Variables are writable; that is their purpose.

sampleQuestions.question: An API specification should be designed and agreed before implementation begins. Which approach and artefact support this?
options: API-first design using a RAML or OAS specification
Writing the Mule flows first and documenting afterwards
Deploying to CloudHub and iterating in production
sampleQuestions.explanation: API-first means the specification is written and agreed first, then used to generate the implementation scaffolding.
whyWrong: A database schema describes storage rather than the API contract.
Documenting after the fact is the opposite of API-first.
Iterating in production is not a design approach.

sampleQuestions.question: Which component processes a large input in configurable chunks with per-record error tracking?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Batch jobs are designed for large datasets, splitting records into blocks and recording success and failure per record.
whyWrong: For Each iterates a collection within a single flow without batch-level record tracking.
Choice routes conditionally between paths.
Scatter-Gather sends the same event down multiple routes in parallel.

sampleQuestions.question: A flow must call three independent services at the same time and combine their responses. Which router fits?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Scatter-Gather executes routes concurrently and aggregates the results.
whyWrong: First Successful tries routes in order until one succeeds.
Choice selects a single route based on a condition.
Round Robin sends each event to one route in turn.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of the Anypoint Exchange?
options: To monitor CPU usage on CloudHub workers
To publish and discover reusable assets
sampleQuestions.explanation: Exchange is the catalogue where reusable assets are published and found.
whyWrong: Logs are accessed through Runtime Manager and Monitoring.
Runtime metrics are shown in Anypoint Monitoring.
Error handling is defined in the application, not in Exchange.

sampleQuestions.question: Which tool is used to apply policies such as rate limiting and client ID enforcement to a deployed API?
sampleQuestions.explanation: API Manager is where an API is managed at runtime, including applying policies through the gateway.
whyWrong: Design Center is for designing specifications.
Studio is the development environment.
MUnit is the testing framework.

sampleQuestions.question: A developer needs to write automated tests for a Mule flow, including mocking an outbound connector. What should they use?
sampleQuestions.explanation: MUnit is the testing framework for Mule applications and supports mocking processors.
whyWrong: Monitoring observes a running application rather than testing it.
Batch jobs process data; they are not a test harness.
A Logger writes diagnostic output and does not assert behaviour.

sampleQuestions.question: Where should an environment-specific value such as a host name be held?
options: In a property file referenced by the configuration
In a flow variable set at deployment
sampleQuestions.explanation: Externalising values into properties lets the same application move between environments without code changes.
whyWrong: Hard-coding forces a code change for each environment.
The payload carries business data, not configuration.
A flow variable is set per event and is not deployment configuration.

sampleQuestions.question: What does the Transform Message component produce?
options: A RAML specification for the API
A deployment artefact for the application
A reconnection strategy for the connector
A payload or variable value, defined by DataWeave
sampleQuestions.explanation: Transform Message runs DataWeave and writes the result to the payload or to a target variable.
whyWrong: Specifications are authored in Design Center or a text editor.
Deployment artefacts are produced by the build.
Reconnection strategies are connector configuration.

sampleQuestions.question: A connector intermittently fails because the downstream service is briefly unavailable. Which configuration addresses this directly?
options: An increase to the payload size limit
sampleQuestions.explanation: Reconnection strategies retry connectivity failures, which suits a service that is only briefly unavailable.
whyWrong: Batch processing changes how records are handled, not connection reliability.
Payload size is unrelated to availability.
Routing does not address a connectivity failure.

sampleQuestions.question: In which order does a Mule application handle an error raised inside a Try scope that has an On Error Propagate handler?
options: The handler runs, then the error is re-thrown
The error is logged and ignored
The error is swallowed and the flow continues normally
sampleQuestions.explanation: On Error Propagate executes its handler and then passes the error up, so the enclosing scope also fails.
whyWrong: Propagation is more than logging; the error continues upward.
A handled error does not stop the application.
Swallowing the error is On Error Continue behaviour.
